input.brief: Reservas en rojo: Spanish documentary journalism about access to blood in Piura

direction.name: The name as a monument
direction.idea: The name is the headline. Set it so large that it becomes architecture: as wide as the viewport, cropped by an edge, or stacked to fill the screen. Nothing else on the first screen competes; the description of what this is drops to a single small sentence. The idea comes from treating the name's letters as material. Ask what the subject can do to its own name: a photograph of the work sits inside a counter or replaces a letter, the name repeats down the page like a reel, the letters are split to opposite corners and the page happens between them. In the study this was the single most common device among sites scoring 7.5 or more.
direction.composition: First screen: the wordmark spans 88–100% of the viewport width (font-size 16–24vw, set with a clamp so it never wraps), anchored either to the bottom edge with its descenders nearly touching it, or dead centre with everything else pushed to the corners. One line of supporting text at 16–20px sits in a corner on a shared margin; navigation is three or four words in the opposite corner. After the hero the page is deliberately small and calm: a narrow text column or a simple two-column grid, so the contrast with the monument holds. The name returns once more at full width as the footer, in the inverse colours. Margins are tight (20–32px) so the type reaches the edges. Two type sizes do nearly all the work: the monument and a small text size, with one mid size for section headings.
direction.typography: One family. The display cut must survive enormous sizes: tight tracking (-0.04 to -0.07em), leading 0.8–0.9, optical kerning on. Section headings are modest (28–40px) on purpose.
direction.colour: Two values carry the page (ground and ink). The accent, if used at all, appears on one thing only: the single action or the inset image frame. The footer inverts ground and ink.
direction.imagery: Few images, used as inserts in the typography rather than as illustrations beside it: one photograph inside or behind the name (a 4:5 or 1:1 frame replacing a letter, or tucked between two words), then a short run of large full-width or half-width photographs further down. Square corners. No collage of small thumbnails.
direction.richness: Scale. The size of the name against the smallness of everything else is the entire visual event, so protect both ends: do not shrink the name to make room, and do not let body text creep above 20px.
direction.pitfalls: A long name set small is just a logo. If the name has more than about 12 characters, stack it on two lines or crop it with the viewport edge; never drop below 12vw. Do not add a second big headline under the name. Do not decorate the letters.

hero.name: Name under a photograph
hero.blueprint: A full-bleed photograph fills the top 58% of the 1440×900 viewport, touching the top, left and right edges, `object-fit: cover`, with its focal point in the upper two-thirds. The lower 42% is a flat ground colour that butts against the photograph with no gap. The name runs across this band on one line, spanning all 12 columns between 24px margins, at clamp(120px, 19vw, 300px), tracking -0.05em, line-height 0.85, its baseline 28px above the bottom edge so descenders nearly touch it. Fit the size to the length of the name so it never wraps. In the strip of ground between photograph and name, 24px under the photograph's edge, sits one row at 17px: the supporting sentence on columns 1–5 at the left margin, and the single action as a small solid rectangular button flush to the right margin. Navigation is four text links at 15px laid over the photograph's top-right corner, 24px in, with a neutral scrim behind that row only if the image is light there. No logo is repeated: the name is the logo. Nothing else is on the screen.
hero.mobile: The photograph takes the top 50svh at full width, re-cropped around its focal point. The name sits under it at 23vw on one line; a name longer than seven characters breaks onto two lines at 21vw, line-height 0.85, and fills the band down to a 16px bottom margin. The supporting sentence at 16px and the action button stack above the name on the left margin. The links collapse to one 'Menu' word over the photograph, top-right.
hero.headline: The name itself on one line, up to about 12 characters at 19vw (drop towards 13vw for longer names), and at most two lines on a phone.

photos.title: Fog and quiet
photos.note: misty, muted, minimal landscapes and empty horizons; calm areas for text

photos.alt: Wooden steps with railings descending into pale pink fog
Gulls perched on a concrete wall beside a pale still sea
Layered hill ridges fading into warm beige mist
Still blue lake with a faint distant shoreline in haze
Small boathouse at the end of a jetty on dark water at night
Tiny sailboat on a calm sea with distant hills, black and white
Gravel path leading to a cluster of bare trees on a hill
Small red-roofed church below a mountain under a blank white sky

motion.name: Scaling wordmark
motion.description: The giant name responds to the scroll: as the first screen leaves, the wordmark scales down a few percent (or grows from 0.94 to 1 as the footer arrives) on a scroll-linked timeline, so the monument feels heavy. Travel stays under 8%. Static fallback where scroll timelines are unsupported. Recipe: 'Scroll-linked progress' in references/motion.md, animating `scale`.

sections.name: Band of unequal panels
sections.blueprint: A modest heading, then one wide band of pictures. The heading, two to four words at 36–44px, starts at column 3, left of centre, with 64px beneath it. The band spans the full viewport width edge to edge and is 68svh tall: four photographs standing side by side with no gaps and deliberately unequal widths, a flex row with flex-grow values of 5, 2, 3 and 2. Each panel is cropped with object-fit: cover to a tall slice, so the band reads as one folded view. The first panel carries a two-line title at 28px in paper colour at its top-left, 24px in, over a neutral scrim that covers only that corner. Hovering a panel raises its flex-grow to 6 over 500ms while the others give way; without hover the widths simply stay. One caption line at 16px sits under the band at the left margin.
sections.mobile: The heading sits on the margin at 28px. The band becomes a two-by-two block with no gaps, 84svh tall in total: the first row split 64/36 and the second 36/64, so the slices stay unequal. The title stays on the first panel. No hover behaviour.

sections.name: Prints dropped on the headline
sections.blueprint: A flat colour field 100svh tall. A two-line headline of two to four words in an ultra-condensed or ultra-heavy face is centred, each line clamp(120px, 14vw, 210px) tall with leading 0.85. Two portrait photographs, each about 26vw wide at 3:4 with an 8px solid white border like a print, are absolutely placed on top of the headline's centre: one rotated −8 degrees, one +6 degrees, overlapping each other by a third and hiding roughly half the letters, so the eye completes the words. A third, smaller print (16vw) may sit at the lower right, cropped by the section's bottom edge. One plain sentence at 16px sits at the bottom-left margin, 24px from the edges. The prints are above the type in the stacking order; hovering one brings it to the front and straightens it to 0 degrees over 200ms. Nothing else is on the field.
sections.mobile: Headline lines at 30vw, still two lines, centred in a 78svh field. Two prints only, each 52vw wide, rotated −6 and +5 degrees, overlapping at the headline's centre. The small sentence sits at the bottom-left margin at 15px.

sections.name: Giant word, filled bar rows
sections.blueprint: Sized for a reading column 520–640px wide, or centred at that width on a full page. The heading is one word (menu, hours, prices) in tall condensed capitals, its `font-size` set in container units (around 46cqw for four letters, tuned per word) so the letters fill the column from edge to edge, leading 0.8. 20px below, a stack of full-width filled bars, each 56px tall with 6px gaps, in a flat tone one step from the ground, with square corners or a 6px radius. Each bar carries a category name at 16px in medium weight at the left with 18px padding and a plus sign at the right. A bar opens in place as a `details` element: it keeps its fill, and its panel lists items at 16px, name left and price right-aligned with tabular figures, 14px between items, 20px padding. Six to nine bars; the first is open by default.
sections.mobile: The column is the full width with 16px margins, so the one-word heading spans the screen. Bars are 54px tall with 6px gaps and open the same way. Item descriptions, if any, sit under the name at 14px in the soft ink.

sections.name: Lines that step across
sections.blueprint: The sequence is written, not counted. Four lines of display type, one stage per line, each a complete short clause that begins with its order word: 'First you send it.' 'Then we take it apart.' 'You choose one.' 'It ships on Friday.' Set at clamp(36px, 4.6vw, 76px), leading 1.0, one line each. The first line starts on column 1 and each following line starts two columns further right (grid-column-start 1, 3, 5, 7), so the block descends as a staircase and the eye follows the diagonal. Under each line, on that line's own left edge and 12px below, a sentence of up to 34ch at 17px in the soft ink. 56px between stages. The last line may take the accent colour as the single emphasis. The first line serves as the heading; there is no title above. Leave the columns to the left of the final stage empty.
sections.mobile: Lines drop to 8.4vw and may wrap onto a second line. The staircase becomes a smaller indent of 6vw per stage, so the fourth line starts 18vw in. Each sentence sits under its line at 16px on the same indent. 40px between stages.

sections.name: Big names, fixed preview
sections.blueprint: Project names are the index. In columns 1–8, five to nine names stack one per line at clamp(44px, 5.4vw, 80px), leading 1.0, each row a link with 10px of vertical padding. All names rest in the ink at 35% opacity except the active one, which is full ink; the first is active by default, and hover or keyboard focus moves the state. To the right of each name, on its baseline at 14px: the discipline and the year. In columns 9–12 a `position: sticky; top: 15vh` frame, 4:5 and 26vw wide with square corners, shows the active project's photograph; all images are stacked in the frame and swapped by opacity over 200ms. A two-word heading at 28px sits top-left, 48px above the first name. Nothing is drawn between rows: the size of the type and the dimming do the separating.
sections.mobile: Names at 9.5vw, all in full ink, one per line; discipline and year sit beneath each name at 13px. There is no sticky frame: each name is preceded by its own photograph at 16:10, full width, so the list becomes image then name, repeated, with 40px between projects.

sections.name: Right-half paragraph, lone photo
sections.blueprint: No heading. On a 12-column grid with 5vw margins, one statement paragraph of 45–70 words occupies columns 7–12 only, set at clamp(24px, 2.2vw, 34px) with leading 1.25 and a first-line indent of 3em. Its top edge sits 18vh below the section top. Columns 1–6 stay empty except for a single square photograph, 20vw wide, in columns 1–3, placed so its top aligns with the paragraph's last line and it hangs below the text by most of its height. A five-line note at 14px, 180px wide, sits in columns 1–2, 96px beneath the photograph. Section padding is 160px top and bottom. Nothing is centred: the paragraph's left edge is the midpoint of the page, and later text blocks on the page may reuse that line. Holds one paragraph, one photograph and one note.
sections.mobile: The paragraph comes first at 22px, full width with 20px margins and no indent. The photograph follows at 62% width, pushed to the right margin, in a 4:5 crop instead of square. The small note sits to its left, bottom-aligned with the photograph, in the remaining 30% of the width.

sections.name: Side facts, wide paragraph
sections.blueprint: Two rows share one vertical line at 34% of the viewport width. Row one: in a 160px column at the left margin, three label and value pairs stack with 20px between them, each a label in the soft ink with its value beneath in full ink, all at 13px (founded, based in, team size). From the 34% line a five-line paragraph at clamp(20px, 1.7vw, 26px), leading 1.35, runs to 90% of the width. Row two starts 120px lower and repeats the logic for the record of the practice: one plain word at 13px at the far left (awards, press, clients), then from the 34% line two list columns, each 260px wide with a 64px gutter, at 13px with 10px between lines: name at the left, year at the right in the soft ink. No heading; the paragraph opens the section. Each list comfortably holds 6–12 lines. No photographs are needed.
sections.mobile: Everything aligns to the left margin. The paragraph comes first at 19px. The three label and value pairs follow as a two-column grid at 14px. The two record lists stack with 40px between them, each opened by its plain word in full ink.

sections.name: Name first, places under it
sections.blueprint: The wordmark opens the footer instead of closing it. On a full-bleed field in the page's inverse or final chapter colour, the name spans the full content width as the first thing, its cap line pushed 8% above the footer's top edge so the tops of the letters are sliced off by the section (`overflow: hidden` and a negative top margin in `em`). 72px beneath, a two-part row: columns 1–5 list the places or ways to reach the studio (cities, or email and telephone), one per line at 32–36px in the accent ink, each a link; columns 7–12 hold three columns of small links at 15px, top-aligned with the first place. A final row 96px lower carries the legal line at the left and a back-to-top text link at the right, both 13px. The field is about 90svh tall, and nothing sits between the wordmark and the row but space.
sections.mobile: The sliced wordmark stays at the top, fitted to the width. Places follow as a list at 26px, then the link columns two across at 15px. Legal line and back-to-top link share the last row at 12px, at opposite margins.

references.name: Paul Kalkbrenner
references.idea: Swiss poster typography for a techno artist: the name as one black line with a photo set inside it like a glyph, then every chapter gets its own flat colour and visible grid.
references.hero: Pure white viewport. The artist's name sits on one line at exact vertical centre in bold black neo-grotesk, about 10.4vw, spanning roughly 78% of the width with equal side margins. The space between first and last name is replaced by a small landscape black-and-white photo, x-height tall and resting on the baseline. Top-left is a tiny circular monogram; eight nav links in 13px bold are spread at even intervals across the right half of the top edge. Bottom edge: equaliser bars with a grey label over a track title at left, a three-line bold blurb starting just left of centre, a sound toggle hard right. About 85% is empty.
references.type: ABC Diatype Plus Variable only: bold at -0.05em tracking for display and 13.5px bold for everything functional. Display runs from 150px in the hero to about 44vw elsewhere per the digest. Tiny uppercase labels inside boxed cells; no second face, no italics.
references.colour: #ffffff #000000 #c5c5c5 #a7ff9c #ff6831 — Black on white to start, then whole sections flood with flat mid-grey, acid mint and orange. Photos inside coloured sections are tinted to the section hue or kept black-and-white.
references.imagery: Portraits and live shots of the artist: full-bleed colour images between sections, a grainy monochrome portrait marked up as a vinyl disc, a green duotone car portrait, and a strip of small mixed-ratio thumbnails. Square corners throughout.
references.layout: Outer margins of only 4-8px; content hangs on a visible column grid with hairlines and boxed cells. Sections alternate between full-bleed photographs and flat colour fields, each arranged differently, so the rhythm is one poster after another.

sections.description: Two words stacked in bold grotesk at roughly 8vw, each preceded by a solid black circle about the height of the lowercase, the second line indented further right than the first. Thin horizontal and vertical hairlines cross the white field at baselines and column edges like a construction grid. Directly beneath is a single row of streaming-service logos spaced evenly edge to edge, then a full-bleed photograph.

Flat mid-grey field split in two. Left half: a square grainy monochrome portrait with a large thin circle drawn on it and a small grey dot at the centre, so the photo reads as a record. Right half: a row of three year tabs and a small link above a hairline, the album title in small bold caps, a short description lower down, and along the bottom two wide outlined cells side by side acting as buttons.

Acid-mint field introducing the tour list. A large photograph, recoloured as a green-and-black duotone, occupies only the top-right quadrant; the left half is left empty. Along the bottom a table header with three tiny uppercase column labels sits on a hairline spanning the full width, where the list of dates begins.

Orange field. A horizontally scrolling strip of small photographs of differing widths runs across the top, cropped by both edges. Below it one outlined rectangle spans the width, divided into three equal cells: two inputs and a submit action, each identified only by tiny centred uppercase text. Small-print lines sit under the left and right cells.

steal: Replace the space between the two words of a giant name with a small photo cropped to x-height.
Flood each chapter with one flat colour and tint its photograph to match as a duotone.
Build forms and button pairs as adjoining outlined cells with tiny uppercase labels instead of filled buttons.
references.media: The hero is almost pure type: the only picture is a 113x75 chip set inside the name, under 1% of the fold, that changes photo every 1-1.5s. Later, full-bleed bands with scrubbed parallax between sections, a square cover in one half beside an info column, a green duotone portrait docked right, a full-bleed photograph that exits through a pixel-block mask, a receding stack of square photos, and an auto marquee of small thumbnails; one YouTube embed, no native video, square corners and an 8s grain overlay.
references.motion: There is no preloader, only the name chip cycling and the equaliser bars bouncing, and Lenis and Barba run 12 ScrollTriggers with no pins: media wrappers parallax by yPercent, a ruled statement drifts sideways, full-bleed photo sections scrub at 0.3 to drive the pixel-block dissolve, and year digits roll like an odometer. Link characters roll over 0.5s with a per-character delay on the house curve cubic-bezier(.625,.05,0,1) (.7s and .35s tokens).

references.name: Kereliott
references.idea: A quiet house gets a quiet page: one dark field, one typeface, the name set as wide as the screen and photographs left to drift in generous darkness.
references.hero: Very dark green-black field with cream type. A two-line introductory sentence at about 30px sits top-left inside 30px margins; a small cream rectangular button sits top-right. The upper half is otherwise empty. The house name fills the full content width in a flared humanist sans, mixed case, with capitals about 19vw tall, its baseline at roughly 87% of the viewport height. Immediately beneath, separated by a gap of a few pixels, the top sliver of a full-width landscape photograph enters from the bottom edge.
references.type: A single face, Trust, in regular weight: a humanist sans with flared terminals and old-style figures. The wordmark is an oversized graphic; all other text is one size of about 20-30px plus tiny 10px photo captions. Hierarchy is position, not weight.
references.colour: #161c1a #eae8dc #222926 #1f2926 — Cream on green-black from top to bottom with no accent colour. The map is drawn in a tone barely lighter than the ground, so photographs supply all the colour.
references.imagery: Natural-light photos of a stone cottage, garden and deck with square corners, in mixed portrait and landscape crops at differing sizes. One full-width opener, then small images placed singly with tiny captions under the left corner.
references.layout: 30px margins, text held to the left 60% in one size. Photographs are staggered left and right at different widths with large dark gaps between, like pictures passed on a wall. The name and a booking button stay fixed in the top corners.

sections.description: A full-width landscape photograph runs margin to margin directly under the wordmark, followed after a gap by a four-line paragraph in the single text size, left-aligned and spanning about 85% of the width. There is no heading or label; the text simply continues the sentence begun at the top of the page.

After a left-aligned paragraph, a silhouette map of the region sits centre-left, about half the viewport wide, filled in a green only a few percent lighter than the background. Five towns are marked with small ring dots and tiny labels; only the house's town has a solid cream dot. No border, legend or frame.

Photographs are placed one or two per screen in a stagger: a portrait image about 30% wide against the left margin, a larger near-square one starting lower against the right margin, later a landscape image top-right of centre and a smaller one bottom-left. Each has a 10px caption under its left corner. More than half of every screen is empty dark ground.

Two short left-aligned sentences in the standard text size with underlined inline links to booking platforms and an email address, then a small cream certification badge. The footer is a single line at the very bottom: social link left, copyright centre, three underlined utility links right, with a tall empty gap above.

steal: Size the wordmark to fill the content width exactly and let the first photograph tuck directly under its baseline.
Draw a location map as a tone-on-tone silhouette with one filled dot among ring dots.
Use a single typeface in one weight and essentially one text size, creating hierarchy through placement and emptiness.

references.name: 21 Hrs On The Moon
references.idea: An explorable Apollo 11 landing site: a title screen where the word MOON sets behind the lunar horizon, then a draggable top-down surface map with hotspots and a mission timeline.
references.hero: Black starfield framed by thin bronze corner brackets; three small round icon buttons top-left. A centred composition 72% wide sits between two thin rules. The upper rule is interrupted by a small bold caps kicker; beneath it the four-letter title in bold geometric caps at 20.8vw spans the full width, light grey fading to transparent at its base. A grey cratered sphere rises from the bottom, its curved horizon overlapping the lower quarter of the letters. On the sphere: a two-line centred white sentence, with a mono-labelled mission name at far left and year at far right above the lower rule. A bracketed mono button sits centred at 82% height.
references.type: Futura Std Bold in uppercase at 300px with -0.03em tracking for the title, the same face near 28px for the kicker and 20px for the sentence; Akkurat Mono in tiny uppercase for labels, the button and map annotations. Roughly a 15x jump from title to sentence.
references.colour: #020202 #262626 #d8d8d8 #8a7361 #ffffff — Black and lunar greys with white type. A muted bronze appears only in the HUD brackets and translucent wedge markers on the map; archival photo thumbnails add small spots of colour.
references.imagery: A real-time 3D moon: curved horizon on the title screen, then a full-screen top-down cratered surface lit from one side. Small archival photos appear as thumbnail hotspots with bracketed corners; icons sit in outlined circles and squares.
references.layout: A single-screen application rather than a scrolling page: a centred title card, then a draggable map filling the viewport with hotspots at fixed coordinates. HUD brackets, icon buttons at top-left and a timeline ruler along the bottom persist throughout.

sections.description: Full-viewport top-down lunar surface in dark grey with fine crater relief. About ten hotspots are scattered over it: outlined circular icons for panoramas, each with a translucent bronze wedge showing the camera's field of view; small square icons for experiments; two photo thumbnails with corner brackets. Each has a tiny mono caps label to its right. One landmark gets a larger bold geometric caps label with a small triangle above it. A tiny mono hint sits top-centre.

Pinned along the bottom, a horizontal ruler spanning about 75% of the width: a thin baseline with short vertical ticks dividing eight equal segments, each labelled in two lines of tiny mono caps, a small triangle marking the current position and a clock readout at the left end. The current landmark's name in bold caps sits beneath it, half-cropped by the bottom edge of the screen.

steal: Let a 3D or photographic object physically overlap the bottom of giant title letters and fade the letters to transparent there, so the type sits inside the scene rather than on top of it.
Interrupt a thin horizontal rule with the small first line of the title, then close the block with a second rule carrying two labelled facts at its left and right ends.
Frame the viewport with four thin corner brackets in a muted metallic colour to turn a full-screen scene into a viewfinder.
references.media: The hero is all picture: a starfield and a rising moon sphere over the lower ~55%, with the title sunk into its horizon. After landing, a draggable top-down terrain map fills the whole screen, with 120x90 archival photo thumbnails as pins and translucent field-of-view wedges; no video on the surface, as footage and panoramas open from the hotspots.
references.motion: There is no document scroll: the first wheel step plays a landing in which the terrain lights up and the hotspots arrive in a stagger, labels after their icons, and from then on the wheel does nothing and the map is dragged instead. HUD items fade in and out on a uniform 400ms, with one opacity .3s cubic-bezier(.61,1,.88,1); no GSAP, and the page took 38s to reach network idle.
